help.energy: Energy is the electricity estimated from CPU, memory, disk and network use. kWh measures accumulated energy: 1 kWh equals 1,000 W used for one hour. The value refers to the selected period, not instantaneous power.
help.emissions: CO₂e (carbon dioxide equivalent) estimates emissions associated with the electricity used by the application. The calculation combines estimated energy with the region’s carbon factor. It is not a direct measurement of the application’s emissions.
help.coverage: Coverage is the share of the analyzed time supported by usable data. At 100%, the entire period is covered. Energy and CO₂e can have different coverage. A gap means missing information, not zero consumption.
help.states: Available means valid metrics; Unavailable means a failed query; No metrics means missing readings; Removed means confirmed departure from the source registry. New checks update the state while history is preserved.
help.metrics: CPU, memory, disk and network describe application resource use and feed the energy estimate. Check the observation time: an update attempt can fail and retain the previous reading. A valid zero differs from a missing reading.
help.factor: The regional factor describes emissions associated with each kWh of electricity in that region. The same energy can produce different CO₂e values with different factors. Calculation records identify the factor and methodology used.
help.period: The period is the time window analyzed, not the collection frequency. Granularity, where available, is the size of reading groups, such as an hour or a day. Check the displayed time zone when reading dates.
help.composition: Each bar or slice shows an application’s share of calculable CO₂e in the selected scope. A larger share means a larger contribution to the total; it does not by itself establish lower efficiency. Missing data is not treated as zero.
